shared.default_view: Open at M0. Show each change and its short energy/wider-context card automatically; advancing remains user-controlled.
shared.replay_policy: Load target scene/data; never accumulate fuel or energy on replay. Do not change the water packet. No new compulsory task or score.

shared.heatwave: Contextual question only; no numerical weather control or annualized stress-event forecast.

optional_questions.question: Does 10 MW mean the whole building?
optional_questions.answer: No. It is the authored average IT demand. With PUE 1.20, the modelled annual-average facility demand is 12 MW. Peak demand and connection rating remain unknown.

optional_questions.question: Is all the extra electricity used for cooling?
optional_questions.answer: No. The non-IT budget also includes power-conversion losses and other supporting systems. PUE alone cannot separate cooling.

optional_questions.question: Will nearby homes lose electricity?
optional_questions.answer: This packet cannot determine that. A service assessment needs peak loads, network topology, available capacity and protection requirements; an annual energy budget cannot predict household outages.

optional_questions.question: Do we need a new substation?
optional_questions.answer: That is not established. Service assessment may identify cables, transformers or other reinforcement. The schematic illustrates that possibility without selecting a real route, upgrade or construction impact.

optional_questions.question: Would clean electricity remove the need to assess the grid?
optional_questions.answer: No. SF has different electricity procurement and delivery arrangements. The physical connection still needs assessment; this campus has no confirmed supply contract or network capacity allocation.

optional_questions.question: What happens in hot weather or drought?
optional_questions.answer: Hot weather can increase regional cooling demand. The campus response depends on its actual equipment and controls. No heatwave electricity or drought-water multiplier is applied; annual averages are not stress-event predictions.

optional_questions.question: Could we save water with another cooling system?
optional_questions.answer: Potentially. The energy consequence depends on technology and conditions. No matched SF alternative has been established here, so the demo explains the choice without displaying invented water or electricity savings.

cards.title: Operation — servers and supporting systems
cards.animation: Start schematic servers. Split incoming electricity into IT and supporting systems; show inherited cooling make-up and blowdown beside it.
cards.what_changed: The campus now has a full-year normal-operation electrical budget.
cards.why: IT uses electricity; cooling, electrical losses and other supporting systems add to the facility budget.
cards.meaning: At the selected PUE, supporting systems add 20% to IT electricity and make up one-sixth of facility electricity. This is not a cooling-only measurement.
cards.uncertainty: The transferred PUE is a design-based teaching assumption. Peak demand, local headroom and actual Polo performance are unknown.
visible_assumptions: 10 MW average IT; no further utilization multiplier.
Cooling make-up 1.25 L/kWh IT; annual averages, not hot-day peaks.
